clue.text: Raw new soldiers fighting for the experience of a lifetime

indicators.note: soldiers fighting are thrown about in a melee, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the three words are used letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Fresh recruits go into battle and get an unforgettable adventure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The experience of a lifetime' sounds like a thrill; read cryptically it is the weary cynicism a long life leaves behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Long years of disappointment produce a jaded tiredness with life, the weary result of living a long time.

clue.text: Significant scoreline got Bilbao rocking

indicators.note: a crowd rocking the stadium suggests these letters being shaken into a new order

parts.note: the two words are used letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A football result that matters set the Basque city of Bilbao alight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoreline' suggests a football result; here it is a line in a musical score. An obbligato is an instrumental part that must not be omitted.
explanation.definitionFit: In music an obbligato is an essential accompanying melody, a line of the written score the performer may not leave out.

clue.text: Something part-way through cellular variation

indicators.note: the answer sits partly inside each of the two words, running through the middle of the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the end of cellular and the start of variation

explanation.surface: Something caught midway through a biological change at the level of cells.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the answer is concealed across the two words, and it is also a creature halfway through its transformation.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's grub stage comes between egg and adult, a stage part of the way through its metamorphosis.

clue.text: Wagon being mostly converted to mobile home

indicators.note: a wagon converted is rebuilt into something else, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, all five letters

indicators.note: most of the word but not all of it, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A wagon is being converted, nearly done, into a home on wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: A Winnebago is an American brand of motorhome, now a generic name for a large camper van.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand name is used generally for a large motor caravan, a vehicle that serves as a home on the road.

clue.text: She needs a long time to capture knight

parts.note: ages is an informal phrase for a long time
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a woman's given name, so a pronoun for a female person stands for it.

clue.text: List old lines covered by make up

parts.note: to make up a story is to invent it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Make up' looks like cosmetics; it is the verb meaning to fabricate.
explanation.definitionFit: An inventory is a complete itemised record of goods or stock, a list of items.

clue.text: Endless sport embodies universal tedium

indicators.note: to embody is to contain within, so the letter goes inside
with no ends, so the first and last letters of the game are removed

parts.note: tennis is a sport

explanation.surface: A never-ending game sums up the boredom everyone feels.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French borrowing for listless boredom and weariness, the same as tedium.

clue.text: Dubious sort of marketing advantage held by group

indicators.note: the group holds the advantage, so it is placed inside

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dubious' looks like an adjective but with 'sort' it makes a noun: a person under suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspect is a person thought possibly guilty, someone of questionable character.

clue.text: Uncertainty US student group raised around charge list

an if is a doubt, as in no ifs or buts

explanation.surface: Doubt surrounds an American fraternity whose list of fees has been increased.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a published schedule of prices or duties, a list of what is charged.

clue.text: A doctor's hesitation is a warning sign

explanation.walkthrough: Amber is the traffic light that warns drivers the signal is about to change.
explanation.definitionFit: The amber traffic light cautions drivers to stop, so it serves as a warning signal.

clue.text: Odd times lacking substance

explanation.definitionFit: A non-event is an occasion that proves dull or insignificant, an occurrence with no real content.

clue.text: Copy — one I'm returning to gallery

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

parts.note: the contraction without its apostrophe
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of major British art galleries, the best known in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to mimic or reproduce, which is what copying does.

clue.text: Take action about new teacher retiring early today?

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: dawn is the early part of today.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunrise is the first light of the day, the very start of today's hours.

clue.text: Con German woman leading her country

explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' looks like a verb at the start; it is the noun, a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A con is a confidence trick, a deception meant to cheat someone, which is a fraud.

clue.text: Converse of infernal place to run

explanation.walkthrough: 'Converse' looks like the logical opposite; it is the verb meaning to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourse is to talk at length on a subject, to hold a conversation.

clue.text: Fidel perhaps losing face: relative putting name forward's a high-flier

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, so its first letter is lost

explanation.walkthrough: CASTRO loses its first letter to give ASTRO; in AUNT the N (name) is put forward to give NAUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut travels into space, flying higher than any pilot, so is literally a high-flier.

clue.text: Long-distance image maker flying to the pole

indicators.note: letters flying about land in a new order

parts.note: the three words are used letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A long-range camera is taken on a flight to the North Pole.

clue.text: Discover how to amuse, replacing one half of ascent with the other

indicators.note: one stretch of the word is swapped out for another

explanation.walkthrough: ASCENT splits into ASC and ENT; ENTERTAIN has ENT at its start, and 'the other' half, ASC, replaces it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out something for certain, a synonym of discover.

clue.text: Supporter pays proceeds of crime back

explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan or sponsor; here it is a stool that supports the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A footstool is a low stool that props up a seated person's feet, literally a supporting piece of furniture.

clue.text: Sharpens view of cold country surrounded by adversaries

the US is a country

clue.text: Craft constructed by unknown number of Germans

parts.note: y is an algebraic unknown
acht is German for eight

explanation.surface: A boat built by an uncertain count of German workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A yacht is a sailing or motor vessel, a kind of watercraft.

clue.text: Some selfless attorney held up hanging
